excerpt: The methodological note explains that every subset S is evaluated across all bipartitions, the minimum information bipartition MIB(S) is the bipartition where normalized effective information reaches a minimum, and the corresponding value is Φ(S). Complexes are then subsets with Φ>0 that are not included within a subset having higher Φ, and the complex with the maximum Φ(S) is the main complex.
overview: This is the operational rule connecting the theory's phenomenological commitments to a computable quantity. It establishes why Φ is tied to the weakest informational link: if a subset can be decomposed across a low- or zero-information partition, it cannot function as one integrated subject. The rule also explains why the theory treats subject boundaries as emergent from integration rather than anatomical labels.
title: Minimum Bipartition Defines Φ
